scoring: Each case has a SPEC (the docstring or a ground truth computed independently) and a PREDICTION of what the probe does. Observed outcome classes: HOLDS (probe agrees with SPEC), DEFECT (probe contradicts its docstring or a stated repo rule or an independent ground truth, on in-scope input), LIMIT (probe misbehaves only outside its stated scope or at a regime its bound line names), UNDEFINED (spec silent; behaviour recorded). A prediction CONFORMS if the observed class equals the predicted class.

Q5_slopes.design: slopes: 1/phi, sqrt2-1, sqrt3-1, 1/sqrt2, e-2, pi-3, -1/phi, phi (slope > 1), 2/5, 1/2, 1, 0, 3, 100, 1e-6, and 150 random irrationals in (-3,3). Canonical width via strip_window_1d bounds. For the first eight irrational slopes also scan r = |n - m s|/(1+s) for |m|,|n| <= 6.
predict: P1: canonical width gives exactly 2 distinct gap lengths for every irrational slope tested (including the 150 random ones); never 3. Any 3 would be a float or boundary artefact and gets reported.
P2: rational slopes give 1 or 2 lengths at canonical width, never more.
P3: for each irrational slope s tested in the scan, every convergent error delta_k = |q_k s - p_k| (k >= 0, in range) appears as a two-length width w = r(1+s), and so does w = 1+s (r = 1).
P4: for the golden slope the two-length scan widths are exactly r = phi^k; for other slopes the two-length widths are NOT powers of phi.
P5: where the count is 3, three_gap_sum passes at tol 1e-6 for all of them.
